keyVerseText: And this day shall be unto you for a memorial; and ye shall keep it a feast to the LORD throughout your generations; ye shall keep it a feast by an ordinance for ever.
rootMeaning: The Hebrew word זִכְרוֹן (zikrôwn) derives from the root זָכַר (zâkar), which fundamentally means to remember, make mention of, or bring to remembrance. This root conveys the idea of marking something so that it is recognized and recalled, extending beyond mere memory to an active, intentional remembrance. Thus, זִכְרוֹן carries the sense of a tangible or formal reminder—something established to keep the memory alive, whether a day, object, or record.
usageInScripture: The term זִכְרוֹן appears 24 times in the Hebrew Scriptures, consistently conveying the concept of a memorial or reminder. It is often translated as 'for a memorial' or 'of memorial,' highlighting its use in contexts such as commemorative days, objects, or written records that serve to recall significant events or divine acts. This usage underscores its role as a means to preserve memory within the community, whether through physical symbols like altar-plates or through formal observances like feast days.
theologicalSignificance: Understanding זִכְרוֹן is vital for grasping how God instructs His people to remember His works and covenant faithfulness. Memorials are not mere historical markers; they are divinely ordained aids to faith, prompting ongoing recognition of God's saving acts. This word reveals that remembrance in Scripture is active and communal, shaping identity and worship across generations. In the Christian faith, such memorials prefigure the ultimate remembrance found in Christ, who fulfills and transcends all types of memorials by His atoning work and resurrection, ensuring that God's covenant and salvation are eternally remembered.
keyVerseReflection: Exodus 12:14 states, 'And this day shall be unto you for a memorial; and ye shall keep it a feast to the LORD throughout your generations; ye shall keep it a feast by an ordinance for ever.' Here, זִכְרוֹן signifies that the Passover is established as an enduring reminder of God's deliverance. The word emphasizes that this observance is not simply a ritual but a perpetual, divinely commanded act of remembering, ensuring that God's saving deeds remain vivid and formative for all generations.
